author: Vampinity
note: Upstream's EDEN_NX2_FRAMES_AHEAD=2 (lethevimlet/oot-bc250 73f7b83c1: a present waits for the PREVIOUS frame only, also while the GPU is behind; 13.6 -> 21.3 fps on his BC-250 Kokiri walk). Our core reads the value by its first character: '2' is taken as 0, the full frame wait, so =2 must NOT be put in an env here. The same behaviour is in every build since T87 as EDEN_NX2_FRAMES_AHEAD=1 + EDEN_UP_AHEAD_ALWAYS=1 (nx2_gsv.h: it drops the second wait of the 'GPU is behind' case, which is exactly his two changed lines). Arms, play env v2.5-fast with EDEN_GPU_TIME=1 and the copy guard EDEN_UP_AHEAD_GUARD=3 in both: g control, a + EDEN_UP_AHEAD_ALWAYS=1; w0 is a WARM-UP (first run on the GPU_TIME shader store of this build), then 3 runs each in turn. Earlier (T87-T91, parked): glitches in 4 of 4 always-ahead runs (5-13 moments against 0-2 for the guard alone), fps -1.0, +2.4, +0.5, +2.1 against the same-batch control. Since then: guard copy fixes, skip stale uploads, GBB's guards. Judge BOTH: fps in the fly-over and the door walk, and with check.py 'glitches in N of M runs' per arm: always-ahead widens the window the guard has to cover. It goes into a play env only if it is faster by more than the spread AND glitches in no more runs than the control. Read also the present fence wait in the GPU_TIME lines: his fell from 25 ms to 0. [11 Nov 04:20, on T120: the warm-up is gone (the store is warm from the live plans); every run has EDEN_TEST_DISCARD_SAVE=1 and the item the runner flag --discard-save-reuse, so the save goes back before the first run only. T120 is about 0.9 fps under T116; both arms are on it, so the comparison holds. The live plans gave always-ahead +1.43 fps (village) and +1.66 (pond) with the guard on: this batch counts the glitch runs.]
